item.title: Eckart’s Luncheonette to Close After 115 Years in Westhampton Beach
item.description: Eckart’s Luncheonette, a longtime Westhampton Beach fixture, will close after 115 years in business, with its final day set for Feb. 17. Read More

item.title: How Bridgehampton Turnpike Went from Dirt Toll Road to Major Thoroughfare
item.description: The Bridgehampton Turnpike connects Main Street Bridgehampton to Sag Harbor. It runs for almost six miles through the woods nearly straight as an arrow and is one of the oldest roads in the Hamptons. It was created in Colonial Times as a dirt track because the colonists in the Hamptons needed to import and export... Read More

item.title: Southampton Financial Advisor Gets 6 Years in Prison for $1M Fraud
item.description: An ex-financial advisor from Southampton was sentenced on Jan. 29 to six years in federal prison for bilking a couple out of more than $1 million that he spent on luxurious shopping sprees and country club memberships. Jeffrey Slothower had been convicted of wire fraud, investment advisor fraud and money laundering following a three-day-long trial... Read More

item.title: East Hampton Town Residents Brave Cold & Snow to Score Discounted Beach Parking Permits
item.description: In what has become an annual rite of passage, East Hampton Town residents lined up by the hundreds on a frigid Thursday morning in late-January to purchase discounted parking permits for East Hampton Village beaches. item.title: Local Artists Honor Bob Dylan
item.description: Bob Fest, a live tribute celebrating the music of Bob Dylan, took place at The Clubhouse in East Hampton. The evening featured performances by a lineup of local artists interpreting Dylan’s influential catalog. The event brought the community together to honor Dylan’s lasting impact on music, songwriting, and cultural expression through live performance. Read More
